questions.question: What is the proper footwear for riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels can catch on things. Tuck in your laces so they don't get caught.

questions.question: In traffic, how much stopping distance do motorcycles need compared to cars?
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the same stopping distance as cars in traffic.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use sharp pressure on the front brake to keep the front tire from locking.
Use only one brake at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes. Squeeze the front brake lever slowly and use gentle pressure on the rear brake to avoid locking the front wheel.

questions.question: Motorcycles are hard to see at night. What should a rider do?

options.text: Stay directly in front of another vehicle to be seen in their headlights.

questions.explanation: Ride slower at night and increase your distance from other vehicles. Use your headlight on high beam when not following or meeting another vehicle. Stay flexible about your lane position.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time while riding?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your fingers near the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your fingers near the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Keep your fingers near the clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time. This is especially important when riding through areas where hazards are likely.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: Applies some rear braking when the front brake is used.
Applies some front braking when the rear brake is used.
Applies equal braking to both front and rear when either is used.
Remembers how hard the rider usually brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies some front braking when the rear brake is used.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system applies some front braking whenever you use the rear brake. Check your motorcycle's manual for details about your specific braking system.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black lettering or symbols are warning signs. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What collects in the center of a traffic lane?

options.text: The safest area for motorcycles to travel.
Areas where drivers are least likely to see motorcycles.

questions.explanation: The center of a lane is where debris and oil from cars collect. Hazards like utility hole covers are also found in this area.

questions.question: What braking mistake do most crash-involved riders make?

options.text: They don't brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
They brake the front tire too much and don't brake the rear tire enough.
They only use the front brake.
They only use the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: They don't brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
questions.explanation: Most riders in crashes don't brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.

questions.question: What percentage of riders killed in motorcycle crashes had been drinking?
questions.explanation: Alcohol causes many motorcycle crashes, especially fatal ones. Studies show that about 40 percent of riders killed in motorcycle crashes had been drinking.

questions.question: To prevent fatigue on a long ride, which should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue, dress to protect yourself from wind and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day and take a break at least every two hours. Avoid artificial stimulants because you may feel extremely tired when they wear off.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: The front and rear brakes have equal power.
The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.
Use only the front brake when stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's stopping power. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which does proper riding clothing NOT offer?
questions.explanation: Proper riding clothes protect you from injury in a crash and from weather problems like heat or cold. They do not cause discomfort.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should always be avoided?

options.text: No part should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No part should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: There is no lane position that is always best and no position that should always be avoided. Choose your lane position based on current riding conditions.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: At the front of the group.
Near the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This prevents them from falling behind the group and allows experienced riders to watch them.

questions.question: When riding in traffic, a motorcycle operator should:

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane.
Change lane position based on riding conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride in the left part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lane position based on riding conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: Which vest or jacket color helps you be seen the most?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like red, orange, yellow, or green to be more visible. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: To swerve, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip toward your turn direction.
Press the handgrip away from your turn direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward your turn direction.
questions.explanation: To swerve left, press the left handgrip, then press the right to straighten. To swerve right, press the right handgrip, then the left.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Stay in one part of the lane at all times.
Change your lane position as conditions require.
Always ride in the center so others see you better.
Ride in a zigzag pattern so drivers notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position as conditions require.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Move your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding to the side near the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding far to the other side may encourage the driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle or a motorcycle with a sidecar, why should you not ride too far to the right of your lane?

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will not be able to pass other vehicles as easily.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar sits on the right side of a motorcycle. Riding too far to the right can cause the sidecar to run off the road. On a three-wheeled motorcycle, the rear right wheel may also leave the road if you get too close to the right edge.

questions.question: In a slow, tight turn, what should the rider do?

options.text: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean in the opposite direction of the motorcycle and the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright while your body leans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, you should lean at the same angle as your motorcycle. However, in slow, tight turns, you should keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane give a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane provides three paths of travel for motorcyclists: the left, center, and right portions of the lane.

questions.question: If it starts to rain while you are riding, what is a good idea?

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane has oil deposits that make it dangerous when wet. When rain starts, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. Slow down on wet surfaces.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at the minimum?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride for safety. Check hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week.
